hints.title: Yearly Order Aggregation
hints.text: Extract the year from purchase_date and filter product-year combinations having at least 3 orders.

hints.title: Consecutive Year Pairing
hints.text: Join the qualified yearly orders with itself on the same product_id where second year equals first year plus 1.

hints.title: Deduplicating Product Identifiers
hints.text: Select distinct product_id values from the joined relation.

hints.title: Consecutive Year Orders Query
hints.text:
```sql
WITH YearlyOrders AS (
  SELECT product_id, YEAR(purchase_date) AS yr
  FROM Orders
  GROUP BY product_id, YEAR(purchase_date)
  HAVING COUNT(order_id) >= 3
)
SELECT DISTINCT y1.product_id
FROM YearlyOrders y1
JOIN YearlyOrders y2
  ON y1.product_id = y2.product_id
 AND y2.yr = y1.yr + 1;
```

complexity.time: O(N log N) to aggregate orders by product and year, followed by self-join
complexity.notes: Group-by filters out non-qualifying years early before self-join.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Examining individual order dates directly without grouping by year leads to slow window lookups.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Intermediate CTE stores qualifying (product_id, yr) pairs.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate aggregates orders per year with having clause, then matches consecutive year records.

solutions.approach: CTE Aggregation with Consecutive Year Join
solutions.code:
WITH YearlyOrders AS (
  SELECT product_id, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM purchase_date)::INT AS yr
  FROM Orders
  GROUP BY product_id, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM purchase_date)::INT
  HAVING COUNT(order_id) >= 3
)
SELECT DISTINCT y1.product_id
FROM YearlyOrders y1
JOIN YearlyOrders y2
  ON y1.product_id = y2.product_id
 AND y2.yr = y1.yr + 1;
